```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r model-meta, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
ui <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wu_2026_linezolid"))
cat("* Citation: ", ui$reference, "\n", sep = "")
cat("* Description: ", ui$description, "\n", sep = "")
```

* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2026.1766346>
* Supplement: <https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fphar.2026.1766346/full#supplementary-material>

Wu 2026 develops a one-compartment population PK model for intravenous
linezolid from 20 critically ill adults who received 600 mg every 12 h as a 1-h
or a 3-h infusion, then uses it in Monte Carlo simulations to ask how the
infusion duration (0.5 h to a 12-h continuous infusion) trades efficacy against
trough-driven toxicity. The supplement holds the covariate-selection steps
(Supplementary Table S1) and diagnostic figures; it carries no additional
parameter values or model code.

# Population

Twenty critically ill adults in the Emergency ICU of the First Affiliated
Hospital of Bengbu Medical University, China, were enrolled between January 2017
and January 2021 (Methods 2.1). All received intravenous linezolid 600 mg q12h:
ten as a 1-h standard infusion and ten as a 3-h prolonged intermittent
infusion. Patients on renal replacement therapy were excluded. Blood was drawn
before the first dose and 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 12 h after the start of the
infusion, giving 90 samples per group.

Table 1 reports the two groups separately:

| Characteristic | 1-h infusion (n = 10) | 3-h infusion (n = 10) |
|---|---|---|
| Male / female | 7 / 3 | 4 / 6 |
| Age (years), mean +/- SD (range) | 60.8 +/- 6.1 (51-68) | 55.7 +/- 8.2 (40-67) |
| Weight (kg), mean +/- SD (range) | 65.2 +/- 11.7 (55-96) | 58.9 +/- 4.7 (52-65) |
| Albumin (g/L), mean +/- SD | 44.1 +/- 6.0 | 43.0 +/- 6.9 |
| Cockcroft-Gault CLcr (mL/min), mean +/- SD (range) | 107.2 +/- 14 (71-124) | 99.1 +/- 17.6 (72-128) |

The same information is available programmatically via the model's
`population` metadata (`readModelDb("Wu_2026_linezolid")()$population`).

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each `ini()`
entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Wu_2026_linezolid.R`. The table below
collects them in one place for review.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| One compartment, zero-order input, first-order elimination | n/a | Results 3.2.1 |
| `d/dt(central) <- -kel * central`, dose by IV infusion into `central` | n/a | Results 3.2.1; Methods 2.1 (IV infusion over 1 or 3 h) |
| `vc` equation | `30.7 * (WT/61.5)^2.16` | Results 3.2.2 |
| `cl` equation | `7.37 * (CLcr/106.5)^1.35` | Results 3.2.2 |
| `lvc` | log(30.7) | Table 2, final model, V |
| `lcl` | log(7.37) | Table 2, final model, CL |
| `e_wt_vc` | 2.16 | Table 2, WT_V |
| `e_crcl_cl` | 1.35 | Table 2, CLcr_CL |
| `etalvc` | 0.241^2 = 0.058081 | Table 2, omega V = 24.1%; CV% = sqrt(omega^2) x 100 (Methods 2.2.1) |
| `etalcl` | 0.208^2 = 0.043264 | Table 2, omega CL = 20.8% |
| `expSd` | 0.217 | Table 2, epsilon = 21.7%; exponential residual (Methods Equation 2) |

# Structural verification

The packaged model must reproduce the two printed covariate equations exactly.
Both sides use the same numbers, so the check is gated tightly.

```{r covariate-equations}
mod <- readModelDb("Wu_2026_linezolid")

grid <- tidyr::crossing(
  WT   = c(50, 61.5, 75, 96),
  CRCL = c(60, 90, 106.5, 130)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number())

# One dose and one observation per grid point; observations are on the ODE
# state `central`, never on the algebraic observable `Cc`.
grid_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  grid |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = 600, evid = 1L, cmt = "central"),
  grid |> dplyr::mutate(time = 1, amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)

# zeroRe() removes the etas on purpose, so rxode2's warning that a
# multi-subject solve has no omega is expected and muffled; any other warning
# still surfaces.
muffle_no_omega <- function(w) {
  if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
}

sim_grid <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxode2::rxSolve(
    rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
    events = grid_events,
    keep   = c("WT", "CRCL")
  ),
  warning = muffle_no_omega
) |>
  as.data.frame()

chk_cov <- sim_grid |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, WT, CRCL, cl, vc) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    cl_paper = 7.37 * (CRCL / 106.5)^1.35,
    vc_paper = 30.7 * (WT / 61.5)^2.16,
    cl_rel   = abs(cl - cl_paper) / cl_paper,
    vc_rel   = abs(vc - vc_paper) / vc_paper
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(chk_cov) == nrow(grid),
  max(chk_cov$cl_rel) < 1e-8,
  max(chk_cov$vc_rel) < 1e-8
)

chk_cov |>
  dplyr::filter(WT %in% c(50, 61.5, 96), CRCL %in% c(60, 106.5, 130)) |>
  dplyr::select(WT, CRCL, cl, cl_paper, vc, vc_paper) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "WT (kg)"          = WT,
    "CLcr (mL/min)"    = CRCL,
    "CL model (L/h)"   = cl,
    "CL paper (L/h)"   = cl_paper,
    "V model (L)"      = vc,
    "V paper (L)"      = vc_paper
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits  = 3,
    caption = "Model-computed CL and V against the Wu 2026 Results 3.2.2 equations."
  )
```

The reference patient (61.5 kg, CLcr 106.5 mL/min) has CL = 7.37 L/h and
V = 30.7 L, an elimination half-life of
`r sprintf("%.2f", log(2) * 30.7 / 7.37)` h.

# Replicate Figure 2 -- visual predictive check

Figure 2 is the VPC of the first 600 mg dose given over 1 h (panel a) or 3 h
(panel b). The observed data are not public, so the virtual patients below
draw weight and creatinine clearance from a normal distribution with each
group's Table 1 mean and SD, truncated to the group's observed range. The
predicted medians of Figure 2 were digitised by the maintainers and are shown
as points.

```{r vpc-cohort}
# `set.seed()` seeds R's RNG for the covariate draws. It does not fix
# rxode2's eta draws across machines (those streams are split per solver
# thread), so every assertion below is written to hold for any cohort.
set.seed(20260630)

n_vpc <- 200L

# Normal draws truncated to [lo, hi] by inverse-CDF sampling.
rtrunc_norm <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  p <- stats::runif(n, stats::pnorm(lo, mean, sd), stats::pnorm(hi, mean, sd))
  stats::qnorm(p, mean, sd)
}

vpc_groups <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,         ~dur, ~wt_m, ~wt_sd, ~wt_lo, ~wt_hi, ~cr_m, ~cr_sd, ~cr_lo, ~cr_hi,
  "1-h infusion",    1,  65.2,   11.7,     55,     96, 107.2,     14,     71,    124,
  "3-h infusion",    3,  58.9,    4.7,     52,     65,  99.1,   17.6,     72,    128
)

vpc_subj <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(vpc_groups)), function(i) {
  g <- vpc_groups[i, ]
  tibble::tibble(
    id    = (i - 1L) * n_vpc + seq_len(n_vpc),
    group = g$group,
    dur   = g$dur,
    WT    = rtrunc_norm(n_vpc, g$wt_m, g$wt_sd, g$wt_lo, g$wt_hi),
    CRCL  = rtrunc_norm(n_vpc, g$cr_m, g$cr_sd, g$cr_lo, g$cr_hi)
  )
}))

vpc_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  vpc_subj |>
    dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = 600, rate = 600 / dur, evid = 1L, cmt = "central"),
  vpc_subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = sort(unique(c(seq(0, 12, by = 0.25), 0.5)))) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::select(-dur) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

sim_vpc <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = vpc_events,
  keep   = c("group", "WT", "CRCL")
) |>
  as.data.frame()

stopifnot(nrow(sim_vpc) > 0, !anyNA(sim_vpc$Cc))
```

```{r vpc-figure, fig.height = 4}
# Medians read off Wu 2026 Figure 2 at the nominal sampling times: the
# predicted median (blue line) by pixel colour against the axis box, the
# observed median (red line) by eye.
fig2_dig <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,         ~time, ~pred, ~obs,
  "1-h infusion",   0.5,   8.1,  5.6,
  "1-h infusion",   1,    15.2, 14.2,
  "1-h infusion",   2,    12.3,  9.1,
  "1-h infusion",   3,     9.6,  7.3,
  "1-h infusion",   4,     7.7,  6.5,
  "1-h infusion",   6,     4.7,  5.5,
  "1-h infusion",   8,     3.1,  3.4,
  "1-h infusion",  12,     1.6,  1.4,
  "3-h infusion",   0.5,   2.7,  5.3,
  "3-h infusion",   1,     5.0,  9.0,
  "3-h infusion",   2,     9.0, 11.9,
  "3-h infusion",   3,    12.0, 14.7,
  "3-h infusion",   4,     9.7, 10.8,
  "3-h infusion",   6,     6.0,  7.5,
  "3-h infusion",   8,     4.0,  5.2,
  "3-h infusion",  12,     1.7,  1.7
)

vpc_sum <- sim_vpc |>
  dplyr::group_by(group, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = stats::quantile(sim, 0.05),
    Q50 = stats::median(sim),
    Q95 = stats::quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

fig2_long <- fig2_dig |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(pred, obs), names_to = "series", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::mutate(series = ifelse(series == "pred", "Figure 2 predicted median", "Figure 2 observed median"))

ggplot(vpc_sum, aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), fill = "grey70", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = fig2_long, aes(time, conc, colour = series, shape = series), size = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Figure 2 predicted median" = "blue", "Figure 2 observed median" = "red")) +
  facet_wrap(~group) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after start of infusion (h)",
    y = "Linezolid concentration (mg/L)",
    colour = NULL, shape = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 2 of Wu 2026: simulated median (black) and 90%",
      "prediction interval (grey) of the first 600 mg dose, n = 200 per group."
    )
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r vpc-compare}
vpc_cmp <- fig2_dig |>
  dplyr::left_join(vpc_sum, by = c("group", "time")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    pct_pred = 100 * (Q50 - pred) / pred,
    pct_obs  = 100 * (Q50 - obs) / obs
  )

stopifnot(nrow(vpc_cmp) == nrow(fig2_dig), !anyNA(vpc_cmp$Q50))

# Centre-of-distribution checks: a mis-transcribed V, CL or dose moves the
# whole profile by tens of percent. The bounds leave room for the gap between
# the paper's own predicted and observed medians in the 3-h panel.
stopifnot(
  abs(stats::median(vpc_cmp$pct_pred)) < 30,
  abs(stats::median(vpc_cmp$pct_obs)) < 30
)

vpc_cmp |>
  dplyr::select(group, time, pred, obs, Q50, pct_pred, pct_obs) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Group"                       = group,
    "Time (h)"                    = time,
    "Figure 2 predicted (mg/L)"   = pred,
    "Figure 2 observed (mg/L)"    = obs,
    "Simulated median (mg/L)"     = Q50,
    "% diff vs predicted"         = pct_pred,
    "% diff vs observed"          = pct_obs
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Simulated against digitised Figure 2 medians.")
```

In the 1-h panel the simulated median follows the paper's predicted median
closely through the peak and the elimination phase. In the 3-h panel it runs
about 20-30% above the paper's predicted median and close to the paper's
**observed** median; the paper's own predicted line sits below its observed
data there. The cohort is drawn from the 3-h group's Table 1 covariates
(lighter and with lower CLcr than the 1-h group, so a smaller V and a lower
CL), whereas the paper does not say which covariates its VPC simulations used.
See *Assumptions and deviations*.

# Virtual cohort for the Monte Carlo simulations

The paper simulated 1,000 virtual patients "using demographic variances (Mean
WT = 61.5 kg; Mean CLcr = 106.5 mL/min) derived from the study population"
(Methods 2.4) without stating the SDs. Here weight and CLcr are drawn from
normal distributions with those means and the pooled whole-cohort SDs implied
by Table 1 (9.3 kg and 16.0 mL/min), truncated symmetrically at 3 SD so the
means stay at the stated values. Each infusion duration gets 200 virtual
patients.

Linezolid is linear in this model, so concentrations scale exactly with dose:
each duration is simulated once at 100 mg q12h and rescaled to every dose
level, which means the dose arms of one duration share the same 200 patients.

```{r mc-cohort}
set.seed(20260701)

n_mc  <- 200L
durs  <- c(0.5, 1:12)
doses <- seq(300, 900, by = 100)

wt_sd_pool <- sqrt((9 * (11.7^2 + 4.7^2) + 10 * ((65.2 - 62.05)^2 + (58.9 - 62.05)^2)) / 19)
cr_sd_pool <- sqrt((9 * (14^2 + 17.6^2) + 10 * ((107.2 - 103.15)^2 + (99.1 - 103.15)^2)) / 19)

# Truncation is symmetric (+/- 3 SD) so the cohort means stay at the stated
# 61.5 kg and 106.5 mL/min.
mc_subj <- tibble::tibble(
  id   = seq_len(n_mc * length(durs)),
  dur  = rep(durs, each = n_mc),
  WT   = rtrunc_norm(n_mc * length(durs), 61.5, wt_sd_pool, 61.5 - 3 * wt_sd_pool, 61.5 + 3 * wt_sd_pool),
  CRCL = rtrunc_norm(n_mc * length(durs), 106.5, cr_sd_pool, 106.5 - 3 * cr_sd_pool, 106.5 + 3 * cr_sd_pool)
)

# 14 doses (0-156 h) so that 144-168 h is a full steady-state day, matching
# the paper's 'seventh day (144-168 h)' window. Dosing continues through it.
mc_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  mc_subj |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      time = 0, amt = 100, rate = 100 / dur, ii = 12, addl = 13L,
      evid = 1L, cmt = "central"
    ),
  mc_subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = seq(144, 168, by = 0.1)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_, ii = NA_real_, addl = NA_integer_,
      evid = 0L, cmt = "central"
    )
) |>
  # `dur` is an rxode2 event column (infusion duration), so it must not reach
  # rxSolve alongside `rate`; it is joined back on by id after the solve.
  dplyr::select(-dur) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

c(wt_sd = wt_sd_pool, crcl_sd = cr_sd_pool)
```

# Simulation

```{r mc-simulate}
sim_mc <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = mc_events,
  keep   = c("WT", "CRCL")
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, cl, Cc100 = Cc) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(mc_subj, id, dur), by = "id")

stopifnot(
  nrow(sim_mc) == n_mc * length(durs) * length(seq(144, 168, by = 0.1)),
  !anyNA(sim_mc$Cc100)
)
```

`Cc` is the individual prediction without residual error; the PTA analysis,
like the paper's, uses it.

```{r figure3, fig.height = 6}
fig3 <- sim_mc |>
  dplyr::filter(dur %in% c(0.5, 6, 12)) |>
  tidyr::crossing(dose = c(300, 600, 900)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc = Cc100 * dose / 100) |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose, dur, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q025 = stats::quantile(Cc, 0.025),
    Q50  = stats::median(Cc),
    Q975 = stats::quantile(Cc, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    panel = factor(
      paste0(dose, " mg (DUR = ", dur, " h)"),
      levels = paste0(rep(c(300, 600, 900), each = 3), " mg (DUR = ", c(0.5, 6, 12), " h)")
    )
  )

ggplot(fig3, aes(time - 144, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q025, ymax = Q975), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 6)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after 144 h (h)",
    y = "Linezolid concentration (mg/L)",
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates the steady-state day of Figure 3 of Wu 2026: median and",
      "95% interval, q12h, n = 200 per duration."
    )
  )
```

# PKNCA validation

Steady-state NCA over 144-168 h for 600 mg q12h at five infusion durations,
grouped by treatment. Cmin and Cmax over a 24 h window at steady state equal
those of either 12 h dosing interval.

```{r pknca}
nca_durs <- c(0.5, 1, 3, 6, 12)

sim_nca <- sim_mc |>
  dplyr::filter(dur %in% nca_durs, abs(time * 4 - round(time * 4)) < 1e-6) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Cc = Cc100 * 6,
    treatment = paste0("600 mg q12h, DUR ", dur, " h")
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)

stopifnot(all(c(144, 168) %in% sim_nca$time))

dose_nca <- mc_subj |>
  dplyr::filter(dur %in% nca_durs) |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 156, by = 12)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(amt = 600, treatment = paste0("600 mg q12h, DUR ", dur, " h")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id, concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, amt ~ time | treatment + id, doseu = "mg")

intervals <- data.frame(start = 144, end = 168, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tbl <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result)

stopifnot(nrow(nca_tbl) > 0, !anyNA(nca_tbl$PPORRES))
```

## Comparison against the paper's steady-state equations

Wu 2026 summarises its simulations in Equation 4, an exponential fit of the
steady-state extremes against the infusion duration,
`Cmin,ss = Dose/300 x 0.67 x exp(0.1308 x DUR)` and
`Cmax,ss = Dose/300 x 9.158 x exp(-0.0878 x DUR)`, and states
`AUC24,ss = 0.2687 x Dose` independent of duration (Results 3.3). These are
regressions through the simulated summaries rather than reported NCA, so they
are the reference values here.

```{r nca-compare}
nca_ref <- tibble::tibble(dur = nca_durs) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    treatment = paste0("600 mg q12h, DUR ", dur, " h"),
    cmin      = 600 / 300 * 0.67 * exp(0.1308 * dur),
    cmax      = 600 / 300 * 9.158 * exp(-0.0878 * dur),
    auclast   = 0.2687 * 600
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(-dur)

nca_cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = as.data.frame(nca_ref),
  by        = "treatment",
  units     = c(cmax = "mg/L", cmin = "mg/L", auclast = "mg*h/L")
)

knitr::kable(
  nca_cmp,
  digits  = 2,
  caption = paste(
    "Simulated median steady-state NCA (144-168 h, AUC over 24 h) against",
    "Wu 2026 Equation 4 and AUC24,ss = 0.2687 x Dose."
  )
)
if (!is.null(attr(nca_cmp, "footnote"))) cat(attr(nca_cmp, "footnote"))

# Equation 4 is an exponential curve fitted through simulated summaries, so it
# is not an exact target at every duration. The gate is on the centre across
# the five durations: a mis-transcribed V or CL shifts every row together.
eq4_chk <- nca_tbl |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cmin")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(sim = stats::median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    tidyr::pivot_longer(nca_ref, c(cmax, cmin), names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "ref"),
    by = c("treatment", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * (sim - ref) / ref)

stopifnot(
  nrow(eq4_chk) == 2 * length(nca_durs), !anyNA(eq4_chk$pct),
  abs(stats::median(eq4_chk$pct)) < 15,
  max(abs(eq4_chk$pct)) < 35
)
```

AUC24,ss agrees with the paper's slope to within a few percent at every
duration, as it must for a linear model. Cmax,ss and Cmin,ss agree best at
3-6 h; at the shortest infusions the simulated Cmax,ss is higher and Cmin,ss
lower than Equation 4, because a single exponential in DUR cannot follow the
true duration dependence across the whole 0.5-12 h range that the paper
fitted it to.

```{r auc-closed-form}
# At steady state, AUC over 24 h of q12h dosing is the daily dose / CL for a
# linear one-compartment model. Both sides use the same drawn CL, so this is a
# numerical identity (trapezoid error on a 0.25 h grid) and is gated tightly.
auc_id <- nca_tbl |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::select(id, auc = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::distinct(sim_mc, id, cl), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * (auc - 1200 / cl) / (1200 / cl))

stopifnot(
  nrow(auc_id) == n_mc * length(nca_durs),
  abs(stats::median(auc_id$pct)) < 0.5,
  stats::quantile(abs(auc_id$pct), 0.9) < 2
)

# The paper's AUC24,ss = 0.2687 x Dose is the slope of the simulated
# exposure against dose. 0.2687 sits within 1% of 2 / 7.37 = 0.2714 for the
# typical patient, so a mis-transcribed CL moves the cohort median far
# outside this band.
auc_slope <- stats::median(auc_id$auc) / 600
stopifnot(abs(auc_slope / 0.2687 - 1) < 0.10)
auc_slope
```

# Replicate Table 3 -- composite probability of target attainment

The composite target (Methods 2.5) is met when AUC24,ss/MIC >= 100 **and**
%T>MIC >= 85% (efficacy) **and** Cmin,ss < 8 mg/L (safety). Table 3 splits the
patients who miss it into "above the range" (Cmin,ss >= 8 mg/L) and "below the
range" (efficacy not met and Cmin,ss < 8 mg/L); the three parts add up to 100%.
%T>MIC is computed over the 144-168 h day on the 0.1 h grid.

```{r pta}
mics <- c(0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4)

subj_ss <- sim_mc |>
  dplyr::filter(time < 168 - 1e-9) |>
  dplyr::group_by(id, dur, cl) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    cmin100 = min(Cc100),
    conc    = list(Cc100),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

pta_subj <- subj_ss |>
  tidyr::crossing(dose = doses, MIC = mics) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    auc24  = 2 * dose / cl,
    cmin   = cmin100 * dose / 100,
    ftmic  = mapply(function(cc, d, m) mean(cc * d / 100 > m), conc, dose, MIC),
    over   = cmin >= 8,
    eff    = auc24 / MIC >= 100 & ftmic >= 0.85,
    ok     = eff & !over,
    under  = !eff & !over
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(-conc)

pta_tab <- pta_subj |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose, dur, MIC) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    PTA   = 100 * mean(ok),
    below = 100 * mean(under),
    above = 100 * mean(over),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

stopifnot(all(abs(pta_tab$PTA + pta_tab$below + pta_tab$above - 100) < 1e-8))
```

```{r table3}
# Wu 2026 Table 3, composite PTA (%) for the printed dose / duration cells.
table3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~dose, ~dur, ~`0.125`, ~`0.25`, ~`0.5`, ~`1`, ~`2`, ~`4`,
  300, 0.5, 92.3, 87.9, 76.0, 24.2, 0.4, 0,
  300, 3,   96.6, 92.3, 83.7, 25.2, 0.4, 0,
  300, 6,   99.4, 98.2, 90.8, 26.3, 0.3, 0,
  300, 9,   99.8, 99.8, 93.5, 26.7, 0.3, 0,
  300, 12,  99.2, 99.2, 92.9, 26.1, 0,   0,
  500, 0.5, 95.0, 91.0, 85.8, 67.8, 11.6, 0,
  500, 3,   96.3, 94.0, 89.2, 74.1, 11.2, 0,
  500, 6,   97.2, 96.8, 94.7, 78.1, 10.4, 0,
  500, 9,   94.3, 94.3, 94.2, 77.3, 7.6, 0,
  500, 12,  84.5, 84.5, 84.4, 67.5, 0,   0,
  700, 0.5, 93.3, 90.0, 85.8, 76.9, 33.0, 0.2,
  700, 3,   93.4, 91.8, 88.3, 82.2, 34.6, 0.1,
  700, 6,   91.3, 91.1, 90.1, 86.2, 33.0, 0.1,
  700, 9,   83.0, 83.0, 83.0, 81.1, 24.9, 0,
  700, 12,  52.8, 52.8, 52.8, 50.9, 0,   0,
  900, 0.5, 89.9, 87.4, 83.3, 77.3, 55.4, 3.2,
  900, 3,   88.5, 87.1, 84.6, 79.5, 58.1, 2.9,
  900, 6,   83.0, 82.9, 82.4, 80.0, 55.8, 1.2,
  900, 9,   67.1, 67.1, 67.1, 67.0, 41.7, 0,
  900, 12,  22.4, 22.4, 22.4, 22.3, 0,   0
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(dose, dur), names_to = "MIC", values_to = "PTA_paper") |>
  dplyr::mutate(MIC = as.numeric(MIC))

# Over-exposure (the up-arrow column) does not depend on the MIC.
table3_above <- tibble::tribble(
  ~dose, ~dur, ~above_paper,
  300, 0.5, 0.1, 300, 3, 0.1, 300, 6, 0.2, 300, 9, 0.2, 300, 12, 0.8,
  500, 0.5, 0.4, 500, 3, 1.6, 500, 6, 2.7, 500, 9, 5.7, 500, 12, 15.5,
  700, 0.5, 3.5, 700, 3, 5.3, 700, 6, 8.7, 700, 9, 17.0, 700, 12, 47.2,
  900, 0.5, 7.4, 900, 3, 10.5, 900, 6, 17.0, 900, 9, 32.9, 900, 12, 77.6
)

pta_cmp <- table3 |>
  dplyr::left_join(pta_tab, by = c("dose", "dur", "MIC")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(diff = PTA - PTA_paper)

above_cmp <- table3_above |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::distinct(pta_tab, dose, dur, above), by = c("dose", "dur")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(diff = above - above_paper)

stopifnot(
  nrow(pta_cmp) == nrow(table3), !anyNA(pta_cmp$diff),
  nrow(above_cmp) == nrow(table3_above), !anyNA(above_cmp$diff)
)

pta_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(cell = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", PTA, PTA_paper)) |>
  dplyr::select(dose, dur, MIC, cell) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = MIC, values_from = cell, names_prefix = "MIC ") |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose q12h (mg)" = dose, "DUR (h)" = dur) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Composite PTA (%), simulated (Wu 2026 Table 3 in parentheses).")

above_cmp |>
  dplyr::select(dose, dur, above, above_paper) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose q12h (mg)"          = dose,
    "DUR (h)"                 = dur,
    "Cmin,ss >= 8, simulated (%)" = above,
    "Cmin,ss >= 8, Table 3 (%)"   = above_paper
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Over-exposure (Table 3 up-arrow column).")

# n = 200 per duration gives a binomial SE of up to 3.5 percentage points per
# cell, and cells near a threshold cliff (CI at 700-900 mg) are the most
# sensitive to the unreported covariate SDs. A mis-transcribed CL, V or
# exponent moves whole rows by tens of points.
stopifnot(
  stats::median(abs(pta_cmp$diff)) < 6,
  stats::quantile(abs(pta_cmp$diff), 0.9) < 15,
  stats::median(abs(above_cmp$diff)) < 6,
  stats::quantile(abs(above_cmp$diff), 0.9) < 15
)

tibble::tibble(
  Comparison = c("Composite PTA, 120 cells", "Over-exposure, 20 cells"),
  `Median |diff| (points)` = c(stats::median(abs(pta_cmp$diff)), stats::median(abs(above_cmp$diff))),
  `90th percentile |diff|` = c(stats::quantile(abs(pta_cmp$diff), 0.9), stats::quantile(abs(above_cmp$diff), 0.9)),
  `Max |diff|` = c(max(abs(pta_cmp$diff)), max(abs(above_cmp$diff)))
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Simulated minus Wu 2026 Table 3, percentage points.")
```

The simulated composite PTA follows Table 3 closely, including its central
finding: at 300 mg PTA rises monotonically with infusion duration, while at
700-900 mg it falls steeply beyond about 6 h because the steady-state trough
crosses 8 mg/L (the over-exposure column). The largest differences sit at the
continuous-infusion cells of 700 and 900 mg, where the attainment depends on
how many patients straddle Cmin,ss = 8 mg/L and is therefore most sensitive
to the unreported spread of the virtual covariates.

```{r figure5, fig.height = 4}
pta_tab |>
  dplyr::filter(MIC %in% c(0.25, 0.5)) |>
  ggplot(aes(dur, PTA, colour = factor(dose), group = dose)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(~MIC, labeller = labeller(MIC = function(x) paste0("MIC = ", x, " mg/L"))) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0.5, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(
    x = "Infusion duration (h)", y = "Composite PTA (%)", colour = "Dose q12h (mg)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Wu 2026. n = 200 per duration."
  )
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Covariate centring.** Methods Equation 3 describes the centring value as
  the covariate median, but the final equations (Results 3.2.2) print 61.5 kg
  and 106.5 mL/min, which the Monte Carlo section calls the study-population
  means. Table 1 reports only per-group summaries (whole-cohort means 62.1 kg
  and 103.2 mL/min), so neither description can be checked. The printed
  equation values are used as written.
* **Typical values in the Discussion.** The Discussion quotes CL = 7.06 L/h and
  V = 31.3 L, which match neither the base (6.96 L/h, 30.9 L) nor the final
  (7.37 L/h, 30.7 L) estimates of Table 2. The model uses the Table 2 final
  estimates, which agree with the Results 3.2.2 equations.
* **Input.** Methods 2.2.1 mentions models "with first-order absorption",
  but every dose was intravenous and Results 3.2.1 selects "zero-order input
  and first-order elimination". The model has no depot; doses are infusions
  into `central`.
* **Variability scale.** Methods 2.2.1 defines CV% = sqrt(omega^2) x 100, so
  the Table 2 percentages are the SDs of the etas (omega^2 = 0.241^2 and
  0.208^2). The residual 21.7% is read on the same scale as the SD of the
  exponential (log-normal) residual. No eta covariance is reported.
* **Virtual cohort.** The SDs and truncation of the Monte Carlo covariate
  distributions are not reported; the pooled Table 1 SDs and a symmetric
  3-SD truncation are an assumption. The paper simulated 1,000 patients per regimen; this
  vignette uses 200 per infusion duration and rescales them across doses, so
  Table 3 cells carry a binomial standard error of up to 3.5 percentage
  points.
* **Protein binding.** The Limitations mention "a fixed protein binding
  fraction" but no value is given. The PTA here is computed on total
  concentrations; the published AUC24,ss/MIC pattern (for example near-zero
  attainment at 300 mg and MIC 2 mg/L, where total AUC24 is about 80 mg*h/L)
  is consistent with total rather than unbound exposure.
* **Figure 2 digitisation and VPC cohort.** The Figure 2 medians were read
  off the published image (658 x 241 pixels) at the nominal sampling times
  and carry reading error of roughly 0.3 mg/L. The paper does not state which
  covariates its VPC simulations used; here each panel uses its own group's
  Table 1 weight and CLcr distribution. The resulting 3-h panel matches the
  paper's observed medians more closely than its predicted medians.
* **Erratum search.** No correction notice for this article was found on the
  EuropePMC record of the article, which lists no comment or correction
  (checked 2026-11-14).
